statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-81871 (GHSA-w34q-cm8f-9c5x, GO-2026-6508): the OTLP log gRPC exporter go.opentelemetry.io/otel/exporters/otlp/otlplog/otlploggrpc loads TLS settings from OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_LOGS_CERTIFICATE, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_CERTIFICATE and the client certificate variables, but newGRPCDialOptions does not apply them, so the connection falls back to the system roots without the client certificate and CA pinning or mTLS configured that way is not enforced. It is fixed in otlploggrpc 0.21.0 by commit c65d435, which makes newGRPCDialOptions use the environment TLS configuration for the transport credentials: https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/security/advisories/GHSA-w34q-cm8f-9c5x, https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/commit/c65d435b43e5e6b82310e6b18dd4cdcb8ac63a0c, https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-go/releases/tag/exporters/otlp/otlplog/otlploggrpc/v0.21.0 . The commit is in the exporters/otlp/otlplog/otlploggrpc/v0.21.0 tag and not in v0.20.0. We read every published jaeger-dev package for Alpine 3.24 in the DHI Alpine repository: 21 builds, 2.19.0-r1 to the current 2.23.0-r4, each for x86_64 and aarch64, every download checked against its index checksum. Each package holds one file, /usr/bin/jaeger, a Go program. Its build information lists otlploggrpc v0.19.0 in 2.19.0-r1 to 2.19.0-r4, v0.20.0 in 2.20.0-r0 to 2.20.0-r5 and v0.21.0 from 2.21.0-r0. We read the Go function table (pclntab) of every build with a reader that finds runtime.main and main.main in each of them. otlploggrpc.newGRPCDialOptions, the function the fix changes, is present in every build. In 2.20.0-r5 and 2.21.0-r0 the function table's source paths name otlploggrpc@v0.20.0/client.go and otlploggrpc@v0.21.0/client.go respectively. 2.19.0-r1 to 2.20.0-r5 therefore carry the vulnerable exporter and 2.21.0-r0 is the first fixed build for this owner.
